newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight falls sharply on fresh liquidity.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight falls sharply on fresh liquidity.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell sharply as liquidity improved due to the maturity of a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bill, dealers said on Friday.
They said the overnight rate dipped to 5.8/9 percent at 0815 GMT against a closing of 8.00 percent on Thursday.
The dealers said the interbank rate opened around 7.7 percent and dipped to 7.0 percent before falling all the way to below 6.0 percent in late trading.
Earlier, other interbank rates eased marginally due to the maturity.
They said the maturity helped ease the tightness caused by sustained outflows from the banking system over the last few weeks.
"But, the impact is more psychological. The market is still tight on the whole," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
One-week money was at 7.80/8.00 percent against 8.10/20 and two-week at 7.50/70 percent against 7.80/8.00.
One-month to three-month money was at 7.40/45 percent against 7.45/50, while six-month dipped to 7.45/50 against 7.50/55.
Dealers said the maturity of a 420 million ringgit long-term government bond on April 30 was expected to ease the market further.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange rose across the board, reflecting the change in trend in the spot market, futures dealers said.
At 0830 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was up two points to 92.67, or an implied yield of 7.33 percent.
But, September was up one at 92.66, or 7.34 percent, and December up three at 92.63, or 7.37 percent.
